newsitem.title: USA: Hot IPOs due this week, some strain shows.
newsitem.headline: Hot IPOs due this week, some strain shows.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom should be the hottest initial public offering among some solid new issues this week, but with so many firms tapping the roaring U.S. equity market for cash, signs of strain are begining to show.
German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG will debut Monday on the New York Stock Exchange in a global offering worth roughly $13.5 billion, Europe's biggest ever flotation.

Last week's stellar market debut of Russia's Vimpel-Communications could point to heavy U.S. demand for international telecommunications firms. The stock rewarded investors with a whopping premium of more than 40 percent on its first day of trading Friday, closing at $29.
"(Deutsche Telekom) should rise two points or so at its opening, but it could go up and away into the clouds," said John Fitzgibbon, editor of the IPO Aftermarket.

Barbara Bradley, managing director of syndicate at Laidlaw Equities Inc., said several factors make the IPO attractive: "The company has excellent fundamentals, it's a quality name, and they have very strong backing by underwriters."

Deutsche Telekom American depositary receipts (ADRs) were priced at $18.89 each over the weekend. The offering is the second biggest flotation of stock ever, second only to Japan's Nippon Telegraph & Telephone Corp. (NTT).

However, the IPO of India's BPL Cellular may not have such a strong debut this week. Analysts have said the wireless services provider has had a shaky past financial performance and faces political uncertainty in India.

An international cosmetics company, NuSkin Asia Pacific should also generate strong demand. "This is the best stock on the board this week. They have a proven success formula and they are a cash cow in the international markets," said David Menlow, president of the Springfield, N.J.-based IPO Financial Network.

IPO Maven editor Manish Shah said the stock should benefit from strong Japanese interest as well as under-penetration in the cosmetic market. "These kinds of companies are very profitable. Barriers to entry are very high (for rivals because distribution is expensive. They will do well, although I would get out if the stock shoots through $28," he said.
Other deals that could prosper are MoneyGram and Ticketmaster, analysts say, although Ticketmaster's debut could fare well solely based on its well-known name and despite its weak financials.
"I think if you can hang on to NuSkin and MoneyGram for a year, you'll get some beautiful returns," said Shah.
But the hot deals come tempered by some disappointments.

Hyperion Telecommunications Inc., Giga Information Group, Transcent Therapeutics and sports trading card maker Pinnacle Brands Inc. all cancelled planned IPOs. Other companies, including ViroPharma and multimedia advertising agency Poppe Tyson Inc., cut back estimated proceeds from their planned IPOs.
"It's a bit like what we saw in July," said Menlow, "And this is the market's vain attempt to to keep itself afloat. But there's a big leak -- too many deals and no leadership by any one sector."

But with the equity markets booming and strong demand from choosy investors, who seem to give an edge to issues with strong brand name appeal, some are still willing to brave the waters. New filings are still strong and last week, Martha Stewart, the stockbroker turned queen of tasteful entertaining, decorating and cooking, hinted she might start a chain of retail stores and take it public.
